### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — TargetFramework condition is dead code (AP-21)

**File:** `Directory.Build.props:10`
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (like LibA and LibB), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The SDK only populates it later during the inner build of multi-targeting projects. This condition never matches — `GenerateDocumentationFile` is silently never set.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is evaluated after the SDK has set `$(TargetFramework)`:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Property defaults override project-level settings

**File:** `Directory.Build.targets:6-10`
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` files are imported **after** the project file. Because MSBuild uses last-write-wins semantics, this unconditionally overrides any project-level value. LibB explicitly sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` but it is silently ignored.

**Fix:** Move `TreatWarningsAsErrors` (and other overridable defaults) to `Directory.Build.props` with a conditional default pattern:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — DefineConstants overwrites SDK defaults

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:14`
```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This replaces the entire `DefineConstants` value, erasing SDK-provided constants like `TRACE` and `DEBUG`. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working in Debug builds.

**Fix:** Append instead:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Unquoted condition value

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:13`
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The condition is unquoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty (e.g., during restore or design-time builds), MSBuild evaluates ` == Debug` which is a malformed expression and may produce unexpected results. Additionally, the string comparison will fail if casing differs.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 5. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Incorrect F# source file order

**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj:7-9`
```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** F# is order-sensitive — files are compiled top-to-bottom and can only reference types/modules defined in earlier files. `Services.fs` is listed before `Domain.fs`, so if Services depends on Domain types (which is the typical layering), this will produce `FS0039: The value or constructor is not defined` errors.

**Fix:** Reorder to match the dependency flow (compare with `OrderService.fsproj` which has the correct order):
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

---

### 1. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Legacy `<Reference>` with HintPath to packages folder

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:27-29`
```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a legacy `packages.config`-style reference pointing at a physical `packages/` folder. It should be a `PackageReference` for proper restore, version resolution, and transitive dependency management.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 2. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — PublishOnBuild target re-invokes the project

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:43-45`
```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>

**Problem:** This forks a second build instance of the same project with an additional global property. The two instances share the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath` and can race on file writes, causing intermittent build failures. It also doubles build time.

**Fix:** If publish-on-build is truly needed, use `DependsOnTargets` to chain into the Publish pipeline within the same evaluation:
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);_PublishAfterBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="_PublishAfterBuild" Condition="'$(NoBuild)' != 'true'">
  <!-- publish logic here -->
</Target>
```

---

### 3. `Directory.Build.props` — Analyzer package leaks to consumers

**File:** `Directory.Build.props:17`
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

**Problem:** Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, this analyzer package flows transitively to any consumer of LibA/LibB NuGet packages. Downstream projects would unexpectedly get StyleCop rules enforced.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" PrivateAssets="all" IncludeAssets="runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers" />
```

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:21-22`
```xml
<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
```

**Problem:** SDK-style projects auto-include all `*.cs` files. The explicit `Include` creates a **duplicate item** (CS2002 warning). The `Update` in the same ItemGroup then applies metadata to only one of the duplicates (undefined which).

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` and keep only `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### 1. Hardcoded absolute `OutputPath` in both projects

**Files:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:7`, `LibB/LibB.csproj:7`
```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>

<OutputPath>$(RepoRoot)artifacts\bin\$(MSBuildProjectName)\</OutputPath>
```

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:32-34`

<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** Without `Inputs`/`Outputs`, this target runs on every build — even no-op incremental builds. For a simple `echo` this is harmless but it adds unnecessary work and sets a bad pattern.

**Suggestion:** If it truly should run every time, that's fine. Otherwise, add Inputs/Outputs to participate in up-to-date checks.

Both projects reference packages without centralized version control. As the solution grows, scattered versions become hard to maintain.

**Suggestion:** Add a `Directory.Packages.props` with `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>` and move all `Version` attributes to `<PackageVersion>` items there.

1. **F# `fsharp/` subfolder properly isolates build settings** — The local `Directory.Build.props` and `.targets` are intentionally empty to block C#-specific settings from leaking. This is the correct pattern for mixed-language repos.
